78150-astrology-in-medicine.title: Saints And Signs
78150-astrology-in-medicine.creator: Charles Arthur Mercier, M.D.
78150-astrology-in-medicine.description: A book by Charles Arthur Mercier, M.D.. atest intellects in every age. Albertus Magnus was a convinced astrologer, and even Roger Bacon, that very great man, projected a universal medicine founded upon Astrology. A knowledge of Astrology was a necessary part of the equipment of all educated men; and Astrological terms form to this day an integral part of every European language.

arxiv-2102-12434.title: Linking electrical and thermal conductivity through cross-property inclusion modelling
arxiv-2102-12434.creator: P. A. CilliDepartment of Earth SciencesUniversity of OxfordSouth Parks RoadOxford, OX1 3AN, UK
arxiv-2102-12434.description: Abstract We derive a new cross-property differential effective medium scheme for a composite material’s thermal conductivity as a function of its electrical conductivity and vice versa. Our scheme assumes that one phase is embedded in the other as inclusions. The relations are independent of inclusion volume fraction, but depend on the aspect ratio of the inclusions.

arxiv-2110-14477.title: New Estimates of Rychkov’s Universal Extension Operator for Lipschitz Domains and Some Applications
arxiv-2110-14477.creator: Ziming Shi, Liding Yao
arxiv-2110-14477.description: Abstract . Given a bounded Lipschitz domain Ω ⊂ ℝ n \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n} , Rychkov showed that there is a linear extension operator ℰ \mathcal{E} for Ω \Omega which is bounded in Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. In this paper we introduce some new estimates for the extension operator ℰ \mathcal{E} and give some applications.

arxiv-2207-07063.title: Differential graded Koszul duality: an introductory survey
arxiv-2207-07063.creator: Leonid Positselski
arxiv-2207-07063.description: Abstract . This is an overview on derived nonhomogeneous Koszul duality over a field, mostly based on the author’s memoir [ 64 ] . The paper is intended to serve as a pedagogical introduction and a summary of the covariant duality between DG-algebras and curved DG-coalgebras, as well as the triality between DG-modules, CDG-comodules, and CDG-contramodules.

arxiv-2211-02836.title: The generalized inverses of the quaternion tensor via the T-product
arxiv-2211-02836.creator: Hongwei Jin, Peifeng Zhou, Hongjie Jiang, Xiaoji Liu
arxiv-2211-02836.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hongwei Jin, Peifeng Zhou, Hongjie Jiang, Xiaoji Liu. In this article, specific definitions of the Moore-Penrose inverse, Drazin inverse of the quaternion tensor and the inverse along two quaternion tensors are introduced under the T-product. Some characterizations, representations and properties of the defined inverses are investigated. Moreover, algorithms are established for computing the Moore-Penrose inverse, Drazin inverse of the quaternion tensor and the inverse along two quaternion tensors, respectively.

arxiv-2302-04628.title: Constraining the Temperature-Density Relation of the Inter-Galactic Medium from Analytically Modeling Lyman-alpha Forest Absorbers
arxiv-2302-04628.creator: Li Yang, Zheng Zheng, T.-S. Kim
arxiv-2302-04628.description: Abstract The absorption by neutral hydrogen in the intergalactic medium (IGM) produces the Ly α \alpha forest in the spectra of quasars. The Ly α \alpha forest absorbers have a broad distribution of neutral hydrogen column density N HI N_{\rm HI} and Doppler b b parameter.

arxiv-2303-03484.title: Exact coefficients of finite-size corrections in the Ising model with Brascamp-Kunz boundary conditions and their relationships for strip and cylindrical geometries
arxiv-2303-03484.creator: Nickolay Izmailian, R. Kenna, Vl.V. Papoyan
arxiv-2303-03484.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nickolay Izmailian, R. Kenna, Vl.V. Papoyan. We derive exact finite-size corrections for the free energy F F of the Ising model on the ℳ × 2 ​ 𝒩 {\cal M}\times 2{\cal N} square lattice with Brascamp-Kunz boundary conditions.

arxiv-2305-19683.title: The Quantum Frontier of Software Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study Journal: Information and Software Technology
arxiv-2305-19683.creator: Manuel De Stefano, Fabiano Pecorelli, Dario Di Nucci, Fabio Palomba, Andrea De Lucia
arxiv-2305-19683.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Manuel De Stefano, Fabiano Pecorelli, Dario Di Nucci, Fabio Palomba, Andrea De Lucia. Quantum computing is becoming a reality, and quantum software engineering (QSE) is emerging as a new discipline to enable developers to design and develop quantum programs. This paper presents a systematic mapping study of the current state of QSE research, aiming to identify the most investigated topics, the types and number of studies, the main reported results, and the most studied quantum computing tools/frameworks.

arxiv-2306-06059.title: Semiparametric posterior corrections
arxiv-2306-06059.creator: Andrew Yiu, Edwin Fong, Chris Holmes, Judith Rousseau
arxiv-2306-06059.description: Abstract We present a new approach to semiparametric inference using corrected posterior distributions. The method allows us to leverage the adaptivity, regularization and predictive power of nonparametric Bayesian procedures to estimate low-dimensional functionals of interest without being restricted by the holistic Bayesian formalism.

arxiv-2311-01847.title: The optical absorption in indirect semiconductor to semimetal PtSe 2 arises from direct transitions
arxiv-2311-01847.creator: Marin Tharrault, Sabrine Ayari, Mehdi Arfaoui, Eva Desgué, Romaric Le Goff, Pascal Morfin, José Palomo, Michael Rosticher, Sihem Jaziri, Bernard Plaçais, Pierre Legagneux, Francesca Carosella, Christophe Voisin, Robson Ferreira, Emmanuel Baudin
arxiv-2311-01847.description: Abstract PtSe 2 \rm{PtSe_{2}} is a van der Waals material transitioning from an indirect bandgap semiconductor to a semimetal with increasing thickness. Its absorption threshold has been conjectured to originate from interband indirect transitions. By quantitative comparison between broadband ( 0.8 − 3.0 ​ eV 0.8-3.

arxiv-2402-02434.title: Stability of Schur’s iterates and fast solution of the discrete integrable NLS Thanks: The work of RB in Sections 1, 3, 6 is supported by the Russian Science Foundation grant RScF 19-71-30002. The work of PG in Sections 2, 4, 5 is supported by Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Russian
arxiv-2402-02434.creator: R. V. Bessonov, P. V. Gubkin
arxiv-2402-02434.description: Abstract . We prove a sharp stability estimate for Schur iterates of contractive analytic functions in the open unit disk. We then apply this result in the setting of the inverse scattering approach and obtain a fast algorithm for solving the discrete integrable nonlinear Schrödinger equation (Ablowitz-Ladik equation) on the integer lattice, ℤ \mathbb{Z} .

arxiv-2402-05242.title: On some properties for cofiniteness of submonoids and ideals of an affine semigroup
arxiv-2402-05242.creator: Carmelo Cisto
arxiv-2402-05242.description: Abstract . Let S S and 𝒞 \mathcal{C} be affine semigroups in ℕ d \mathbb{N}^{d} such that S ⊆ 𝒞 S\subseteq\mathcal{C} . We provide a characterization for the set 𝒞 ∖ S \mathcal{C}\setminus S to be finite, together with a procedure and computational tools to check whether such a set is finite and, if so, compute its elements.

arxiv-2403-08011.title: Gujarati-English Code-Switching Speech Recognition using ensemble prediction of spoken language
arxiv-2403-08011.creator: Yash Sharma
arxiv-2403-08011.description: Abstract An important and difficult task in code-switched speech recognition is to recognize the language, as lots of words in two languages can sound similar, especially in some accents. We focus on improving performance of end-to-end Automatic Speech Recognition models by conditioning transformer layers on language ID of words and character in the output in an per layer supervised manner.

arxiv-2403-11105.title: Source Prompt Disentangled Inversion for Boosting Image Editability with Diffusion Models
arxiv-2403-11105.creator: Ruibin Li, Ruihuang Li, Song Guo, Lei Zhang
arxiv-2403-11105.description: Abstract Text-driven diffusion models have significantly advanced the image editing performance by using text prompts as inputs. One crucial step in text-driven image editing is to invert the original image into a latent noise code conditioned on the source prompt.

arxiv-2407-11725.title: Revisiting the Langlie procedure
arxiv-2407-11725.creator: Dennis Christensen
arxiv-2407-11725.description: Abstract Introduced in 1962, the Langlie procedure is one of the most popular approaches to sensitivity testing. It aims to estimate an unknown sensitivity distribution based on the outcomes of binary trials. Officially recognized by the U.S. Department of Defense, the procedure is widely used both in civil and military industry.

arxiv-2408-09275.title: Design and Control of Modular Soft-Rigid Hybrid Manipulators with Self-Contact
arxiv-2408-09275.creator: Zach J. Patterson, Emily Sologuren, Cosimo Della Santina, Daniela Rus
arxiv-2408-09275.description: Abstract Soft robotics focuses on designing robots with highly deformable materials, allowing them to adapt and operate safely and reliably in unstructured and variable environments. While soft robots offer increased compliance over rigid body robots, their payloads are limited, and they consume significant energy when operating against gravity in terrestrial environments.

arxiv-2411-04458.title: Measures of closeness to cordiality for graphs
arxiv-2411-04458.creator: Anand Brahmbhatt, Kartikeya Rai, Amitabha Tripathi
arxiv-2411-04458.description: Abstract A graph G G is cordial if there exists a function f f from the vertices of G G to { 0 , 1 } \{0,1\} such that the number of vertices labelled 0 0 and the number of vertices labelled 1 1 differ by at most 1 1 , and if we assign to each edge x ​

arxiv-2504-18294.title: Secret Sharing in the Rank Metric
arxiv-2504-18294.creator: Johan Vester Dinesen 1 , Eimear Byrne 2 , Ragnar Freij-Hollanti 1 , and Camilla Hollanti 1
arxiv-2504-18294.description: Abstract The connection between secret sharing and matroid theory is well established. In this paper, we generalize the concepts of secret sharing and matroid ports to q q -polymatroids. Specifically, we introduce the notion of an access structure on a vector space, and consider properties related to duality, minors, and the relationship to q q -polymatroids.

arxiv-2511-12580.title: Dynamical Tidal Response of Non-rotating Black Holes:
arxiv-2511-12580.creator: Connecting the MST Formalism and Worldline EFT
arxiv-2511-12580.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Connecting the MST Formalism and Worldline EFT. The response of a black hole (BH) to tidal forces encodes key information about the underlying gravitational theory and affects the waveform of gravitational waves emitted during binary inspiral processes.

pmc-10549984.title: Exposure to Particulate Matter Air Pollution and Age of Menarche in a Nationwide Cohort of U.S. Girls
pmc-10549984.creator: Robert B Hood, Jaime E Hart, Francine Laden, Bernard Rosner, Jorge E Chavarro, Audrey J Gaskins
pmc-10549984.description: Background:It remains unclear whether in utero and childhood exposure to air pollution affects pubertal development, particularly age of menarche in girls.Objective:The aim of this study was to determine whether residential ambient particulate matter (PM) exposure in utero and during childhood is associated with age of menarche.

pmc-10610024.title: COVID-19 Patients’ Medication Management during Transition of Care from Hospital to Virtual Care: A Cross-Sectional Survey and Audit
pmc-10610024.creator: H. Laetitia Hattingh, Catherine Edmunds, Saberina Buksh, Sean Cronin, Brigid M. Gillespie
pmc-10610024.description: Background: Virtual models of care were implemented to ease hospital bed pressure during COVID-19. We evaluated the medication management of COVID-19 patients transferred to virtual models of care. Method: A retrospective audit of COVID-19 patients transferred from inpatient units to virtual care during January 2022 and surveys from patients transferred during December 2021–February 2022 was carried out.

pmc-11528463.title: Breast cancer-derived CAV1 promotes lung metastasis by regulating integrin α6β4 and the recruitment and polarization of tumor-associated neutrophils
pmc-11528463.creator: Qing Lin, Siwen Zong, Yi Wang, Youjia Zhou, Keqin Wang, Fuxiu Shi, Jiayang Wang, Mingrui Feng, Wenting Luo, Lifang Zhang, Hui Lin, Lixia Xiong
pmc-11528463.description: Lung metastasis in breast cancer (BC) patients is one of the main reasons for their high mortality rate. The most prevalent BC small extracellular vesicles (sEVs receptor, integrin α6β4, has been found to interact with surfactant-associated protein (SFTPC) in lung epithelial cells, making BC more likely to metastasize to the lung.

pmc-11642673.title: The Effect of Oil Additives on the Properties of Fly Ash-Based Foamed Geopolymers
pmc-11642673.creator: Barbara Kozub, Jan Dudek, Mykola Melnychuk, Miguel Ángel Sanjuán
pmc-11642673.description: Geopolymers are a modern class of construction materials that show significant potential for sustainable development, especially through the use of industrial wastes such as fly ash. This study investigated the effect of different oil additives on the properties of fly ash-based geopolymers, with particular emphasis on the use of both new and used oils.

pmc-11669519.title: Optimizing active recovery strategies for finger flexor fatigue
pmc-11669519.creator: Dominika Krupková, James J. Tufano, Jiří Baláš
pmc-11669519.description: IntroductionActive recovery (AR) is used during exercise training; however, it is unclear whether the AR should involve the whole body, only the upper extremities, or only the lower extremities when aiming to maintain localized upper body performance. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the impact of different AR strategies on repeated intermittent finger flexor performance leading to exhaustion.

pmc-11691574.title: CHOOSING TO FORGO: LIFE-SUSTAINING TREATMENT DECISIONS FOR SELVES AND RELATIVES AMONG TAIWANESE ADULTS
pmc-11691574.creator: Duan-Rung Chen, Su-I Hou, Yuchi Young
pmc-11691574.description: PurposeSince its implementation in 2019, less than 2% of adults in Taiwan have signed Advance Directives (ADs) under the Patient Right to Autonomy Act (PRAA). This research explores how the public views the PRAA and its effect on the decision to decline life-sustaining treatments (LSTs) in hypothetical end-of-life scenarios.

pmc-11859877.title: A study of the personality trait-focused digital mental health intervention
pmc-11859877.creator: S Jeong, H Kim, S K Lho, S Mun, I Hwang, S Kim, H Lim, H Kim, W Moon, M-S Shin
pmc-11859877.description: IntroductionMental healthcare services that address a variety of primary complaints which are highly related to maladaptive personality traits among the general population are important to prevent developing psychiatric disorders.ObjectivesThis study aimed to examine the effectiveness of a digital mental health service (named “Mindling”) that focuses on maladaptive personality traits in the general population.

pmc-12468588.title: Imaging of Proteinopathies in the Brains of Parkinsonian Disorders
pmc-12468588.creator: Makoto Higuchi
pmc-12468588.description: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), and α-synucleinopathies—including Parkinson’s disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and multiple system atrophy (MSA)—are characterized by the accumulation of misfolded protein aggregates. Advances in positron emission tomography (PET) imaging have enabled in vivo visualization of these pathologies, particularly tau and α-synuclein fibrils, facilitating early diagnosis and differential classification.

pmc-12650637.title: Transcription Factor-Based Differentiation of Pluripotent Stem Cells: Overcoming the Traps of Random Neuronal Fate
pmc-12650637.creator: Georgie McDaid, Jaime Vanek, Brett Cromer, Huseyin Sumer, Gianluca Santamaria
pmc-12650637.description: Developing robust methods to differentiate pluripotent stem cells (PSCs) into specific neuronal subtypes is crucial for advancing neuroscience research, including disease modelling and regenerative medicine. Research in this area has primarily focused on generating and studying excitatory neurons, often in co-culture with primary astrocytes to support maturation.

pmc-12654794.title: Implementation of Replica-Averaged Restraints from Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Measurement with UNRES Coarse Grained Model of Polypeptide Chains
pmc-12654794.creator: Leonid Shirkov, Cezary Czaplewski, Adam Liwo
pmc-12654794.description: We report the implementation of replica-averaged molecular dynamics in the UNRES coarse-grained model of polypeptide chains, with application to the restraints determined by nuclear magnetic resonance. The analytical ESCASA algorithm is used to estimate interproton distances from coarse-grained geometry. With synthetic restraints derived from two selected conformations of the L129–L153 loop of the Slr1183 protein from Synechocystis sp.

pmc-12789786.title: Fenestrated Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins
pmc-12789786.creator: Brenden S. Ingraham, Arashk Motiei
pmc-12789786.description: ObjectiveWe describe a novel approach to transcatheter arterialization of the deep veins (TADV) in a patient with chronic limb-threatening ischemia using the LimFlow kit and a Culotte 2-stent bifurcation technique to maintain peroneal flow while deploying a covered stent graft into the tibioperoneal trunk and posterior tibial vein when there is no tibial artery suitable for the TADV inflow.

pmc-12860157.title: Immersive versus non-immersive virtual reality in improving upper limb function among individuals with subacute hemiplegia: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12860157.creator: Athira George, Sathees Kumar Durairaj, Praveen Kumar Kandakurti, Animesh Hazari
pmc-12860157.description: BackgroundVirtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising tool in neurorehabilitation to improve motor function in individuals with hemiplegia. VR applications are typically categorized into immersive and non-immersive types, both of which have demonstrated efficacy in enhancing upper limb function.

pmc-12955154.title: Highly biased DNA sequence reconstruction in DNA storage with multi-scale attention mechanism and contrast learning
pmc-12955154.creator: Xue Li, Yanfen Zheng, Qi Shao, Jiadong Wang, Wei Li, Bin Wang, Shihua Zhou, Ben Cao, Pan Zheng
pmc-12955154.description: Base substitution, insertion, and deletion errors due to inherent technical constraints inducing unavoidable sequencing inaccuracies, limiting access to high-quality raw data and biological knowledge. To address this, we propose a deep sequence reconstruction model based on the multi-scale attention mechanism and contrastive learning (MACL), designed to enhance DNA sequence reconstruction under highly error rate conditions.

pmc-13388072.title: Prediction models for progression from prediabetes to diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13388072.creator: Yanxian Wang, Cuili Wang, Jianxiu Wang
pmc-13388072.description: PurposePrediabetes increases the risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Accurate prediction is crucial for early prevention, but evidence on prediction models has not been comprehensively synthesized. This study systematically evaluated the accuracy of such models in predicting prediabetes-to-T2DM progression.MethodsDatabases including Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science were searched up to June 2, 2025.

pmc-13559461.title: Staple line coverage with suture fixation of polyglycolic acid patch can reduce postoperative air leakage
pmc-13559461.creator: Yeon Soo Kim, Soorack Ryu
pmc-13559461.description: entioned the possibility that air leakage decreased due to significant advancements in thoracoscopic stapling technology during the nearly 10-year study period. As stated in the paper, only Medtronic products (Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN) were used in the study (2). All of the staples used were Tri-StapleTM purple staples (30, 45, and 60 mm).

pmc-13573397.title: The use of blood test trends in cancer detection: a scoping review
pmc-13573397.creator: Sufen Zhu, Claire Friedemann Smith, Kiana K. Collins, Sheba E. Ziyenge, Jacqueline Murphy, Isabella de Vere Hunt, Zach Brubert, Nia Roberts, Eva J.A. Morris, Richard Hobbs, Brian D. Nicholson, Pradeep S. Virdee
pmc-13573397.description: BackgroundMonitoring trends in repeated blood tests might offer opportunities to improve cancer detection. This review aimed to systematically map the existing literature on blood test trends in cancer detection, characterise how these trends have been used in cancer detection approaches, and identify research gaps.

pmc-13587145.title: Comparative Efficacy of Aldosterone‐Related Sodium‐Retention Pathway Therapies for Resistant Hypertension: A Drug‐Level Network Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmc-13587145.creator: Yi‐Liang Tsou, Yu‐Hung Wang, Yi‐Siou Lin, Chia‐Liang Chen
pmc-13587145.description: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs), aldosterone synthase inhibitors (ASIs), and epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) blockade target different levels of the aldosterone‐related sodium‐retention pathway in resistant hypertension (RH), but the comparative efficacy of individual agents remains uncertain. We conducted a focused drug‐level network meta‐analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing pathway‐directed therapies in adults with RH.
